description: Adds a 2D / 3D compass switch to the Experimental screen. With it on, tapping the compass in navigate mode switches the map between the tilted 3D view and a flat, north-up 2D map the way Google Maps' does, from any state (following you, panned away, paused), and brings the map back to you. The compass shows a single north arrow in 2D, and the next navigation starts in the mode you used last.
name: 2D / 3D compass

description: Removes the "More from this app" label from the account sheet, and keeps the sheet open when you come back from Settings or Customization or tap "Your profile", instead of dropping back to the map.

Remove sign-in prompts, Trim account menu and Remove permissions are left out of this build, Offline saved places keeps only its Local saved screen, which copies your account's saved lists to the phone (Pull from Google account), and its icon carries microG's C. Needs microG: MicroG-RE or ReVanced GmsCore. Not for root (mount) installs.

description: Adds a Better filters switch to the Experimental screen. With it on, the trail filter's sliders move in finer steps over the same ranges: Rating in 0.1 stars (instead of Any, 3.5, 4 and 4.5), Length in 0.1 mi, Elevation gain in 10 ft, Highest point in 100 ft and Distance away in 1 mi (metric: 0.1 km, 5 m, 50 m, 1 km).

description: Reworks the offline area picker: zooming out really selects more instead of being shrunk to Google's size cap, the box can be resized by dragging its edges and corners, a large area is split into several downloads whose true total size is shown, and areas already downloaded are drawn on the map. Can be turned off on the Customization screen.
name: Better offline maps

description: Adds a Better tracking switch to the Experimental screen. With it on, recordings work the way Gaia GPS records: the phone's GPS directly with every fix delivered live (no Play services batching), fixes worse than 65 m or physically impossible dropped, points kept 3 m apart, no trail-biased smoothing, and elevation converted to sea level and counted in 2 m steps.
name: Better tracking

Where Play services rejects the re-signed app, Maps degrades instead of crashing.

Each can be switched back on on the Customization screen.

description: Adds a Location source choice to the Customization screen: Android's own location providers, microG's (microg Services) or Google Play services' fused provider. With Android, neither is ever asked for a location. A source that is missing or disabled is never used, so location keeps working without it. Also keeps the network (Wi-Fi/cell) provider registered when no fused provider answers, instead of GPS only, so a fix does not go stale indoors.
name: Location provider toggle

options.description: The location source Maps starts with. On: the fused provider -- Google Play services', or microG's in microG Maps -- whenever it is installed and enabled, Android's own providers otherwise. Off: Android's own providers. Can be changed later on the Customization screen.

Skipped by Morphe Manager 1.35 and other patcher 1.15+ builds, which would crash Waze when the map opens; patch with Morphe Desktop to get it.

description: Keeps Google Assistant out of Waze: no Assistant button, onboarding or settings entry, whatever Waze's server enables for your region.
name: No Google Assistant

description: Save places without a Google account, kept only on the phone: Save opens Maps' own "Place saved" sheet (Want to go, Travel plans, Starred places, Favorites, your own lists, a note), and a "Local saved" row on the account sheet rebuilds Maps' You tab -- your recent places, your lists and labels (Home, Work, your own) -- with export and import (backup file, KML, Google Takeout's saved lists and Saved Places.json, several files or the whole Takeout .zip at once). It also has a Timeline: where the phone has been, grouped into days and visits, kept only on the phone, with GPX export. Recording is off until switched on there; it shows a notification while it runs. With Add microG support, Maps' own Save keeps syncing to your account and Local saved instead copies the account's saved lists to the phone (Pull from Google account).
name: Offline saved places

description: Brings the Pixel-only power saving mode to every phone: while driving with navigation, press the power button and Maps shows only key information such as the next turn on a black screen. Turn it on or off in Settings > Navigation > Power saving mode. Pixels that have it built in keep Google's own version unless Power saving mode is turned on in Power Saving Options, a row on the account sheet under Customization, which also has: a navigation button that opens the power saving screen without locking the phone, switching to it by itself when idle, a speedometer on it, a lower frame rate, and its black map in navigation or all over Maps.
name: Power saving mode

description: Adds a Proxy screen to Customization that sends Maps' own traffic, map data included, through an HTTP proxy -- for example Orbot's (127.0.0.1:8118) to use Tor. Map data never falls back to a direct connection: if the proxy stops, Maps stops loading. Needs a recent Play services network engine (Cronet); Maps warns when it cannot take the proxy.
name: Proxy

description: Squares off rounded corners across the UI, including the two round navigation buttons.
name: Rectangle shapes

description: Adds a Remember filter states switch to the Experimental screen. With it on, the trail filters you set (length, elevation, rating, difficulty, activities, features and the rest, but not Distance away) stay set when you go back to the home screen and after the app restarts, instead of resetting.
name: Remember filters

description: Removes permissions that only serve Google-account features or Google's data collection: background location, physical activity, contacts, microphone (voice search stops working), camera (Lens and Live View stop working), car speed, advertising ID, push messages and Google services settings. Left out with Add microG support, whose account features need them.
name: Remove permissions

description: Removes Google's sign-in prompts: the first-launch "Make it your map" page, the search screen's "Tired of typing?" card and the account sheet's "Sign in" pill. Tapping "Your profile" (or the pill, where it still shows) answers with a "Can't sign in" toast instead of nothing. Left out with Add microG support, which signs in.
name: Remove sign-in prompts

description: Points the Firebase Installations and Play services compliance check-ins at an unresolvable host, stops every ad impression and click ping from being sent, and deregisters Google's logging, performance-monitoring, survey and Location History libraries and the on-device federated-learning services. With Add microG support, Firebase Installations and Location History are left alone, so Timeline, account sync and push messages keep working.
name: Remove telemetry

description: Turns on Waze's own switch for correcting the speed limit from the speedometer, the old mods' "Report speed limit". Waze's server keeps it off; what it shows is not verified here.
name: Report speed limit

description: Hands the alerts Waze is tracking -- police, crashes, hazards, traffic jams, closures and speed cameras -- to Ungoogled Maps on the same phone, where Waze alerts in Waze Features puts them on the map. Nothing leaves the phone. Waze has to be signed in and open; in the background is enough.
name: Share alerts with Maps

description: Plays the speed camera sound for every camera, not only when you are over the speed limit.
name: Speed camera sound at any speed

description: Chimes and shows a note when a speed or red light camera is coming up ahead, and puts the cameras on the map, from OpenStreetMap. Off until turned on in Waze Features, a row on the account sheet, because it downloads the cameras near you from an OpenStreetMap server -- an area you choose there, about 25 to 175 km across.
name: Speed cameras

description: Turns speed camera and police alerts back on in the countries where Waze's server switches them off. Warning of speed cameras is against the law in some of those countries.
name: Speed cameras everywhere

description: The style of the speed limit sign beside the speedometer, whatever the country.
name: Speed limit sign

options.description: Waze picks one by country.
options.title: Sign style

description: Plays a chime when your speed passes the speed limit during navigation, as Waze does. Maps itself only turns its speedometer red. When it chimes is chosen in Waze Features, a row on the account sheet.
name: Speeding chime

description: Lets Waze keep running in the background without a route for the chosen time -- Waze's server allows 10 minutes -- so that its alerts keep reaching Maps while you navigate there. Costs battery; Waze still closes itself when you close it.
name: Stay awake in the background

options.description: How long Waze may run in the background without a route. Waze: 10.
options.title: Minutes in the background

description: Adds a Theme choice to the Experimental screen: Follow phone, Light, Dark or AMOLED black (dark with pure black backgrounds). AllTrails itself only follows the phone.
name: Theme

description: Removes Your Timeline, Location sharing, Your data in Maps and Help & feedback from the account sheet. Left out with Add microG support, whose account features need them.
name: Trim account menu

description: Shows the alerts a Waze on the same phone is tracking -- police to begin with, and any of crashes, hazards, traffic jams, closures and speed cameras -- as pins on the map, with a chime and a note as one comes up ahead. Off until turned on in Waze Features. Waze has to be patched with Share alerts with Maps, signed in and open; in the background is enough.
name: Waze alerts

description: Adds +, − and reset tiles during turn-by-turn that change the navigation zoom while the camera keeps following the car.

name: Sort by number of ratings

name: Sort by number of ratings

name: Unlock premium

Headset validation pending. Based on @logkim1's 4XVR-GalaxyXR patches: https://github.com/logkim1/4XVR-GalaxyXR.
name: 5.1-channel audio bridge (4XVR)

description: Rewrites native Oculus face/eye permission checks to the Android XR names, on exact 2.0.20/5001712, 2.0.20/5001812, 2.0.21/5001968 and 2.0.22/5002244 builds.
name: Android XR native permission names

description: Legacy overlay fallback for older builds: adds SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and the compositor signal window.
name: Appear on top (legacy)

description: Installs the bundled 5.1-channel AAudio bridge native for exact 4XVR 2.0.22 build 20022. Based on @logkim1's 4XVR-GalaxyXR patches: https://github.com/logkim1/4XVR-GalaxyXR.
name: Audio bridge payload (4XVR)

description: Adds static blue noise after video colour processing and fade, on the background/base layer only; 8-bit or 10-bit input, always 8-bit sRGB output. Selectable per layer, but turn OLED's VD-like fovea options off when combining. Unknown host shaders pass through unchanged.
name: Background blue-noise dithering

options.description: Both choices apply the same final 8-bit output quantizer. This describes your stream; it does not change host negotiation or decoder precision. When combining with OLED calibration, leave both of its existing VD-like fovea toggles off.
options.title: Declared input depth

description: Renames the package and Steam Link's internal VR-launch component, so the patched app can be installed next to the original.
name: Change package name

options.description: Accepts either a full Java package name (for example, com.valvesoftware.steamlinkvr.galaxyxr) or a display suffix (for example, Galaxy XR). Suffix input appends to app name and generates a package suffix automatically.
options.title: Package name

description: Adapts already corrected OpenXR angular velocity to Steam Link 2.0.23's local controller axes. Requires the active Galaxy XR OpenXR Velocity Frame runtime module; do not use with stock runtime velocities or old HAL/velocity/extrapolation APK layers. Changes angular velocity only, not poses, linear velocity or prediction. Exact 2.0.23/5002363 only; headset A/B validation pending. Controller tracking and haptics based on @4uva4ek's Galaxy XR modules: https://github.com/4uva4ek.
name: Controller angular world to local

description: Routes controller vibration to the grip vibrator instead of the trigger, which Galaxy XR uses for every OpenXR vibration. The grip one needs shell rights, so this needs Shizuku running with its permission granted to Steam Link; without it vibration is stock. Controller tracking and haptics based on @4uva4ek's Galaxy XR modules: https://github.com/4uva4ek.
name: Controller grip haptics through Shizuku

description: Makes the Galaxy XR runtime extrapolate controller poses to the time VRLink asks, instead of repeating one sample per display frame, and filters jitter out of the streamed pose. Adds an OpenXR API layer; no Steam Link code changes. Controller tracking and haptics based on @4uva4ek's Galaxy XR modules: https://github.com/4uva4ek.
name: Controller pose extrapolation

description: Takes controller poses straight from the Galaxy XR controller HAL instead of the OpenXR runtime, removing the runtime's ~35 ms sample lag, and filters jitter out of pose and velocity. The HAL needs shell rights, so this needs Shizuku running with its permission granted to Steam Link; without Shizuku tracking stays as it is. Steam Link 2.0.23: angular velocity is reported local to the grip pose. Steam Link 2.0.20 - 2.0.22: angular velocity is reported in the base space. Controller tracking and haptics based on @4uva4ek's Galaxy XR modules: https://github.com/4uva4ek.
name: Controller tracking from the controller HAL through Shizuku

description: Rotates the controller velocities the Galaxy XR runtime reports into the frames SteamVR reads, so thrown objects leave in the right direction. Stock, they arrive in a controller-attached frame. Adds an OpenXR API layer; no Steam Link code is changed. Steam Link 2.0.23: angular velocity is reported local to the streamed pose. Steam Link 2.0.20 - 2.0.22: angular velocity is reported in the base space. Controller tracking and haptics based on @4uva4ek's Galaxy XR modules: https://github.com/4uva4ek.
name: Controller velocity frame

description: Overrides the HMD identity reported to SteamVR. Recommended: Meta Quest Pro on the legacy targets through 5002244. Explicit profiles override that.
name: Device identity

options.title: HMD identity

description: Overrides the HMD identity reported to SteamVR for exact 2.0.23/5002363. Optional; not part of the recommended set. Explicit profiles override that.

description: Bypasses the permission-state gate in XrSceneLobby, on exact 2.0.20/5001712, 2.0.20/5001812, 2.0.21/5001968 and 2.0.22/5002244 builds.
name: Force lobby permission-state gate

description: Bypasses the 3 XR gates in the stream path, on exact 2.0.20/5001712, 2.0.20/5001812, 2.0.21/5001968 and 2.0.22/5002244 builds.
name: Force stream XR gates

description: Adds static blue noise after video colour processing and fade, on the foveal layer only; 8-bit or 10-bit input, always 8-bit sRGB output. Selectable per layer, but turn OLED's VD-like fovea options off when combining. Unknown host shaders pass through unchanged.
name: Foveal blue-noise dithering

options.description: Both choices apply the same final 8-bit output quantizer. This describes your stream; it does not change host negotiation or decoder precision. When combining with OLED calibration, leave both of its existing VD-like fovea toggles off.
options.title: Declared input depth

description: Drains the render dispatch queue before every frame, hands scene switches to RenderDispatch.requestScene instead of the retired render runnable, and routes window teardown through the dispatch for exact 4XVR 2.0.22 build 20022. Headset validation pending. Based on @logkim1's 4XVR-GalaxyXR patches: https://github.com/logkim1/4XVR-GalaxyXR.
name: Frame-synced render dispatch (4XVR)

description: Only for exact 2.0.20/5001812: draws just the foveal image on a transparent 5000x6000 canvas per eye and submits it as the 2nd projection, keeping the background projection and any static trigger quad. Requires headset validation.
name: Full-FOV foveal canvas (experimental)

description: Replaces the four Quest 3 controller assets with the Galaxy XR reference models (2048x2048 textures, re-authored meshes) for exact 4XVR 2.0.22 build 20022. Static asset swap; headset validation pending. Based on @logkim1's 4XVR-GalaxyXR patches: https://github.com/logkim1/4XVR-GalaxyXR.
name: Galaxy XR controller models (4XVR)

description: Permission-free high-resolution fix: appends a static 2x2 Android-surface compositor trigger and leaves each build's native projection layers and formats, including future RGB10_A2, untouched. No image copy. Exact builds 5001712, 5001812, 5001968, 5002244, 5002363.
name: Galaxy XR high-resolution 3-projection fix

description: Installs the Khronos OpenXR loader 1.1.58, the 4XVR view-config API layer and the Galaxy XR manifest declarations for exact 4XVR 2.0.22 build 20022. Decoded-base adaptation; headset validation pending. Based on @logkim1's 4XVR-GalaxyXR patches: https://github.com/logkim1/4XVR-GalaxyXR.
name: Galaxy XR launch compatibility (4XVR)

description: Re-exposes the stock 4XVR launcher artwork under the canonical ic_launcher/ic_launcher_round names (adaptive icon plus density PNGs) and points the manifest at them, matching the Steam Link icon shape for exact 4XVR 2.0.22 build 20022. Based on @logkim1's 4XVR-GalaxyXR patches: https://github.com/logkim1/4XVR-GalaxyXR.
name: Galaxy XR launcher icon (4XVR)

description: Clamps the InitializeDevice refresh-rate picker floors (121.0f/91.0f -> 73.0f) so exact 4XVR 2.0.22 build 20022 requests Galaxy XR's 72 Hz mode. Three guarded bytes in libvr4p-oculus.so; runtime application pending headset validation. Based on @logkim1's 4XVR-GalaxyXR patches: https://github.com/logkim1/4XVR-GalaxyXR.
name: Galaxy XR refresh profile (72 Hz, 4XVR)

description: Installs the Galaxy XR face transport for the VRCFT module, per exact build: the face-tracking bridge layer (XR_FB_face_tracking2 to XR_ANDROID_face_tracking) and the FACE_TRACKING permission on the legacy targets 5001712/5001812/5001968/5002244; the tongue out/left/right/up/down transport slots (keeping Valve's native face expressions and standard TongueOut) on 2.0.23/5002363.
name: GXR face and tongue bridge

description: Installs the modified libplacebo 7.360.1 (LGPL-2.1-or-later), the 4XVR HDR bridge native and the bundled open-source notices for exact 4XVR 2.0.22 build 20022. Based on @logkim1's 4XVR-GalaxyXR patches: https://github.com/logkim1/4XVR-GalaxyXR.
name: HDR pipeline payload (4XVR)

description: Loads the HDR bridge, routes the decoder output surface through it for the FP16 hand-off, detects HLG from the video MediaFormat and keeps the bridge informed of movie/seek transitions for exact 4XVR 2.0.22 build 20022. name: libplacebo HDR pipeline (4XVR)

description: Stubs the 11 exported Oculus platform-init/entitlement/message functions in libovrplatformloader.so of exact 4XVR 2.0.22 build 20022. The reference Galaxy XR build requires the Meta platform channel to stay inert on a non-Meta runtime; launch-criticality is unproven and Meta-store VIP flows degrade. Default off; verify on device before enabling. Based on @logkim1's 4XVR-GalaxyXR patches: https://github.com/logkim1/4XVR-GalaxyXR.
name: Meta platform decoupling (4XVR, experimental)
